_comment: D-42 ratchet baseline. Every (company:scenario) pair whose terminal return exceeds
its cost of capital owes a structured excess_return_defence in the archetype impact
matrix. The pairs below assert one and do not yet declare it, each for a stated
reason. The list may only SHRINK: a pair that acquires a defence must be removed, and
a new undeclared pair fails the test. Same ratchet shape as tests/moat_role_baseline.json
Recorded 16 September 2026, when the D-42 diagnostic was first run. One of the fifteen
valuations asserting an excess return carried a defence at that moment, and it was prose.

Updated 17 Sep 2026. The obligation now triggers on the GOVERNING reading -- the return on the whole capital base where D-49's roll-forward gives one -- which is why dnl:fragmentation appears: it sits below its WACC on new capital and above it on the whole base. dnl:muddle_through and dnl:ai_productivity_lag have LEFT this list, which is the ratchet tightening as intended.

Updated 25 Sep 2026 (D-35/D-36, build order item 4). dnl:fragmentation has LEFT this list: the longer horizon and the revenue-growth fade both narrow the gap between the return-on-new-capital and return-on-whole-capital readings, and Fragmentation now sits (slightly) below WACC on both -- the four-basis-point excess the dnl reason below describes no longer exists. The ratchet tightening as intended.

Updated 2 Oct 2026 (D-71). dnl:fragmentation is BACK on this list: the fixed ten-year horizon holds the flat chain growth four more years, and the whole-base terminal return rises to 9.83% against an 8.88% WACC -- 95bp, no longer the four-basis-point rounding of 25 Sep. Fragmentation has no declared decay horizon (analyses/dnl/five_forces_driver_gap_audit_2026-09-25.md, a genuine gap, not a transcription), so under D-71 it falls back to Gordon on that excess until the five-forces pass assigns one. Baselined on that ground; the gap audit owns the fix.

Updated 2 Oct 2026 (D-72). dnl:stagflation_persists joins: decisions 3 and 4 make it a cyclical scenario (gas spike ends and the margin hit reverts at its own resolution phase, year 5), so by year 10 its whole-base return is 11.8% against an 8.88% WACC. No decay horizon is declared for it (the same genuine gap as Fragmentation), so under D-71 it falls back to Gordon. Baselined pending the five-forces pass.

dnl: dnl:stagflation_persists, under D-72: 11.8% on the whole base against an 8.88% WACC once its cyclical margin hit has reverted. No decay horizon declared (see the gap audit); Gordon fallback, baselined pending the five-forces pass.
dnl:fragmentation, under D-71's ten-year horizon: 9.83% on the whole capital base against
an 8.88% WACC. Not the four-basis-point rounding case of 25 Sep 2026 -- a real 95bp excess
that D-42 says must be defended or baselined. No decay horizon is declared for Fragmentation
(the scenario write-up never assessed terminal ROIC; see the 25 Sep 2026 five-forces gap
audit), so the D-71 headline falls back to Gordon on the earned return, which is the MORE
generous reading. Baselined pending the five-forces pass that assigns the horizon; the
earlier open question (should D-42 carry a materiality floor?) is left as ruled.
Muddle Through, AI Lag, Orderly Convergence and now Disorderly Climate are declared.
wbc: The bank matrix carries no terminal_roic driver for any scenario. In the section 15
fork the terminal return is a DECLARED input on the scenario overlay (terminal_roe)
rather than a matrix cell, so a defence has nowhere to live without deciding where a
bank's terminal-return defence belongs. That is a structural question, not an
omission to be filled in, and it needs Stephen rather than a session.
All six scenarios exceed Ke, by 95 to 295bp.
csl: Do not write a defence for a defect. CSL's 61-73% terminal return on new capital is
an artefact of D-53 being unimplemented: terminal_capex_pct_revenue is declared equal
to da_pct_revenue, so net terminal capex is zero and almost nothing is reinvested.
See M15. Implementing D-53 should drop the implied return into the range DNL occupies
and most of these pairs should leave this list by arithmetic rather than by being
justified. CSL also has no impact-matrix file, so there is no home for a defence yet.
